rows.current: れる
rows.why: CONFIRMED needs-human, but the decision is now narrow and packaged. Certain: れる must not stay. On a godan verb れる is the PASSIVE suffix, and gram:gp-63 (passive) stores the byte-identical forms[0] value れる, so the two records are indistinguishable at the form layer, while gp-115's own already-corrected gloss says the godan potential is the -u to -eru vowel change. Also certain: no kana suffix exists, because the change is a vowel-row shift that keeps the consonant (書ける, 話せる, 飲める, 待てる), and a value like eる would put Latin letters in forms[].form, which has never held them in any of the 498 distinct values across corpus/grammar/n3.json, n4.json and n5.json. The registry already answers this class of problem: gram:gp-127 stores 命令形, gram:ikou-kei-volitional-form stores 意向形, gram:ukemi-kei stores 受身形, all in forms[].form, precisely because those conjugations have no single kana suffix. RECOMMENDED PACKAGE, to accept or reject as one unit, since forms[0] cannot move without the two fields that quote it: forms[0].form becomes 可能形; label.pt-BR becomes forma potencial, "poder/conseguir" (可能形, 〜られる); label.en becomes potential form, "to be able to" (可能形, 〜られる); structure_pattern becomes 可能形. forms[1] られる and its gloss stay untouched. A human owns this because it rewrites two learner-facing label strings, and because the alternative worth weighing is retiring gp-115 as a duplicate of gram:rareru (られる) rather than repairing it.

rows.current: Verbos grupo 1 (godan): troca a vogal -u final por -ō → 行く→行こう, 飲む→飲もう, 話す→話そう, 待つ→待とう. Verbos grupo 2 (ichidan): tira o る e acrescenta よう → 食べる→食べよう, 見る→見よう. Irregulares: する→しよう, 来る（くる）→来よう（こよう）. A versão polida correspondente é a base ます + ましょう (食べましょう).
rows.fix: Oração na forma simples + ようだ: verbo (雨が降っているようだ), adjetivo-い (寒いようだ). Adjetivo-な + な + ようだ (元気なようだ). Substantivo + の + ようだ (夢のようだ). Antes de substantivo vira ような (夢のような話); antes de verbo ou adjetivo vira ように (夢のように). A versão polida é ようです.
rows.why: Upgraded from needs-human to fix. Re-read of corpus/grammar/n4.json confirms the defect is still live and untouched: the whole formation.pt-BR conjugates the VOLITIVO (行く→行こう, 食べる→食べよう, する→しよう, ましょう) inside a record whose label, forms[0] and structure_pattern have all already been corrected to 〜ようだ. Nothing here is a judgement call; it is plain attachment morphology and every clause of the replacement is checkable against the record's own 夢のようだ example. The value differs from the queue's draft only to follow the registry's own wording: adjetivo-い and adjetivo-な are the corpus conventions (39 and 40 uses) against adjetivo-i and adjetivo-na (15 and 10), and forma simples is the dominant term (65 uses).

rows.current: Group 1 (godan) verbs: replace the final -u vowel with -ō → 行く→行こう, 飲む→飲もう, 話す→話そう, 待つ→待とう. Group 2 (ichidan) verbs: drop the る and add よう → 食べる→食べよう, 見る→見よう. Irregulars: する→しよう, 来る（くる）→来よう（こよう）. The corresponding polite version is the ます base + ましょう (食べましょう).
rows.fix: Clause in plain form + ようだ: verb (雨が降っているようだ), い-adjective (寒いようだ). な-adjective + な + ようだ (元気なようだ). Noun + の + ようだ (夢のようだ). Before a noun it becomes ような (夢のような話); before a verb or adjective, ように (夢のように). The polite version is ようです.
rows.why: Same live defect on the en side, same reasoning as formation_pt. い-adjective and な-adjective are the corpus conventions on the en side too (85 and 88 uses against 29 and 32 for the romanized spellings), as are clause and plain form.

rows.current: É CASUAL: entre desconhecidos ou em situação formal, use 〜ましょう. O brasileiro costuma traduzir como imperativo ("comamos!"), mas o tom é mais de convite amigável ("bora comer"). Atenção: sozinha, ela não pede permissão; para isso, liga-se a outras estruturas (ver ようと思う e 〜ようか). Não confunda esse 〜よう volitivo com o 〜ようだ de aparência/comparação; são coisas diferentes, apesar da grafia parecida.
rows.fix: 〜ようだ não é palpite solto: apoia-se em algo que a pessoa percebeu, viu, ouviu ou sentiu. Para repassar o que ouviu de terceiros, use 〜そうだ; para uma impressão visual imediata, 〜そう (寒そう); para conclusão tirada de informação indireta, 〜らしい. Na conversa do dia a dia o equivalente é 〜みたいだ, e 〜ようだ soa mais formal e escrito. A grande armadilha para brasileiros: o 〜よう da forma volitiva (食べよう) se parece na grafia, mas prende-se ao verbo e propõe uma ação, enquanto 〜ようだ vem depois de uma oração inteira e comenta uma aparência.
rows.why: Upgraded from needs-human to fix; the field is still the volitional's nuance word for word (É CASUAL ... use 〜ましょう, comamos!, bora comer), and its register advice is the exact opposite of what this record's own explanation says (É a versão mais formal e escrita de 〜みたいだ). Two corrections to the queue's draft. It called 〜らしい a purely visual impression, which is wrong: 様態 〜そう is the visual impression (寒そう) and 〜らしい is a conclusion from indirect information, so the three contrasts are now separated correctly. And the closing pitfall no longer restates the sentence that stays in explanation.pt-BR after the expl_pt deletion; it adds the attachment difference instead, which is the part a learner actually needs. A grande armadilha para brasileiros is the registry's own phrasing, taken from gram:gp-115.

rows.current: It is CASUAL: among strangers or in formal situations, use 〜ましょう. Brazilians tend to translate it as an imperative ('let's eat!'), but the tone is more of a friendly invitation ('let's go eat'). Note: on its own, it does not ask for permission; for that, it links to other structures (see ようと思う and 〜ようか). Don't confuse this volitional 〜よう with the 〜ようだ of appearance/comparison; they are different things, despite the similar spelling.
rows.fix: 〜ようだ is not a loose guess: it rests on something the speaker perceived, saw, heard or felt. To pass on what you heard from someone else, use 〜そうだ; for an immediate visual impression, 〜そう (寒そう); for a conclusion drawn from indirect information, 〜らしい. In everyday conversation the equivalent is 〜みたいだ, and 〜ようだ sounds more formal and written. The big trap for Brazilians: the volitional 〜よう (食べよう) looks similar in writing, but it attaches to the verb and proposes an action, while 〜ようだ follows a whole clause and comments on an appearance.
rows.why: Same live volitional contamination on the en side, same two corrections as nuance_pt (〜らしい reclassified away from visual impression, closing pitfall no longer duplicating explanation.en). The big trap for Brazilians is the registry's own phrasing, taken from gram:gp-115.

rows.current: "en": "back of the hand"
rows.why: CONFIRMED needs-human, and the queue's escape route is refuted. The gloss defect is real: 手の裏 (てのうら) is the PALM, the same referent as 手のひら (registry entry 6214, palma da mão), while the back of the hand is 手の甲; gloss.pt-BR verso/dorso da mão, gloss.en back of the hand and both translations all say the opposite. But the proposed rescue does not work. I ran the dissector on 紙の裏を見せてください: it does split into 紙 plus の plus 裏, and the 裏 token comes back linked to vocab_id 79, which is 内 (うち) and registers 裏 among its forms, NOT to the declared target 1088 (裏, うら). So 紙の裏 restores a link to the wrong entry and leaves the target unlinked. The human decision is a content decision with no cheap option. (a) Keep 手の裏 and correct gloss plus both translations to palma da mão / palm of the hand, accepting that a sentence tagged 1088 still holds no 1088 link and now teaches a counter-intuitive use of 裏. (b) Re-author the jp to 紙の裏 AND repoint the resulting 裏 token to 1088 by hand, since the form-table lookup will not do it. (c) Retire the sentence and generate a cleaner one for 1088. Whichever is chosen, do not correct the gloss alone: that leaves both translations contradicting it.

rows.current: この問題が解けない学生はない
rows.why: CONFIRMED needs-human, with the renumbering now measured rather than predicted. Ran the dissector on both readings. Stored 学生はない: 8 C tokens, position 7 is ない as 形容詞 非自立可能 with vocab_id 462, exactly as stored, so nothing is wrong against the current jp. Proposed 学生はいない: 9 C tokens, position 7 becomes い (lemma いる, 動詞 非自立可能, vocab_id 69) and position 8 becomes ない (助動詞). The queue's own token edits for this record address position 7, and after the change position 7 is い, not ない, so applying them in either order silently writes the existential note onto the wrong morpheme. The human decision is about what the sentence teaches, not about the parse: the grammar target is gp-102 and the record's structure_explanation teaches the pattern 〜ない〜はない by name, so switching to いない changes the taught surface. 学生はない is nonstandard for an animate subject in modern Japanese, where いない is expected, but it is the literary form of exactly the pattern the explanation names. Whoever decides must also update structure_explanation in both locales and re-issue the position-7 edits against the new numbering.

rows.current: いちにちからあたらしいしごとがはじまる
rows.why: CONFIRMED needs-human, but the queue named a route that does not exist and missed one that does. The named route is closed: scripts/fable5_register_reading_overrides.py registers READING deviations only, and its own docstring and code say structural mismatches are never registrable (structural_mismatches_NOT_registered), so the 10年 and ５月 precedent cannot deliver a boundary merge. The missed route: mode C DOES return １日 as one token read ついたち once a month precedes it. I ran the dissector on ４月１日から新しい仕事が始まる and on 来月の１日から新しい仕事が始まる; both give a single １日 token, reading ついたち, romaji tsuitachi. Bare １日 reads いちにち because the date is genuinely ambiguous without that context, so the analyzer is not wrong, the sentence is underspecified. Second and separate finding: even after the merge the link resolves to vocab_id 56 (一日, いちにち), NOT to the declared target 401 (１日, ついたち), because both entries register both forms １日 and 一日 and dissect.py's _vocab_by_form keeps whichever registered first. So the human decision is two-part. (a) Accept a minimal jp change supplying the month context, which fixes reading, kana, romaji and boundary in one go and is also better Japanese. (b) Decide how 401 gets linked, since the form table cannot separate it from 56; that is a registry-precedence defect that runs past this record. The earlier rejection of つい on １ plus たち on 日 remains correct and must not be revisited.
